slicer board / Overview
Kind

Overview

What this app is

A mobile app for splitting shared costs among a small group of friends: groups, members, expenses, derived balances, and settle-up suggestions. Records and suggests; never moves money.

7Slices shipped
0007Current slice
49Symbols
10Flows

Who it is for

People on a trip or shared activity who need a running tally of who paid and who owes whom. Members are name-slots, not login identities. Someone can be on the ledger without installing the app.

What it can do today

01Create an empty group on device, mint a per-device access token, persist locally, sync group entity to Postgres — slice 0001
02Open a group hub showing id, name, version, and sync status; bump name via merge + wake + fetch — slice 0001
03Reopen groups after app kill from SQLite + Secure Store lobby index — slice 0001
04Auto-flush outbound queue + thin inbound group fetch on group open and app foreground (all lobby groups) — slice 0002
05Add name-slot members, bind this device to one (assumed member), show You (Name) on hub; roster list-pull on open/foreground — slice 0003
06Sync split into flush / apply / subscribe modules behind a groupSync facade; typed clearable errors; queue identity by entity_type + id + version — slice 0004
07Record an expense against the member who paid — integer cents, listed on the hub, synced through the same merge path — slice 0005
08Choose which member you are, and change that choice, until the group's first expense fixes it — slice 0005
09Run the whole app in a browser (npm run web), which is what makes headless end-to-end runs and board screenshots possible — slice 0006
10Split every expense equally across the members live at record time, frozen into the expense, identical on every device — slice 0007
11See each member's net position on the hub — paid minus owed, most-negative first, You (Name) marked — slice 0007
12Reopen a group with several expenses without the screen crashing on revived Date timestamps — slice 0007
13Record a clip per flow and stills for the board with npm run capture, driving the real app against the deployed Edge Functions — slice 0007

Constraints

Rules the build holds to
  • No user accounts (capability tokens prove access)
  • Local-first / full offline, entity-level merge sync
  • Stack: Expo React Native, Expo Router, Legend State, expo-sqlite, Supabase Postgres + Edge Functions + Realtime (wake-only)
  • Remote Supabase project splitnext-v3 (ycpkguwfxlhpovnsuujr, eu-central-1)
  • Access tokens in expo-secure-store
  • Dev/demo: physical phone + Expo Go; npm run web runs the whole app in a browser for testing and screenshots
  • Money as integer cents; version (not timestamps) for conflicts; soft-delete only
  • Device floor iOS 16+ / Android 12+; English-only; light-only UI
  • Clients never talk to Postgres; deny-all RLS; Edge Functions use service role after capability hash-check
  • Slice quality: thin scope, high craft inside the slice (seams + TDD + review); speed ≠ skip quality

Stack

ClientExpo RN 57 + Expo Router — mobile-first; web is a real second target, used for headless testing and board screenshots
UI stateLegend State v3 (useValue, per-group observable) — UI source of truth
Local durabilityexpo-sqlite kv-store via observablePersistSqlite + configureObservableSync — write-through persist; web swaps the plugin for localStorage (persistPlugin.web.ts) because expo-sqlite's web path is wasm over OPFS, which headless Chromium cannot run
Secretsexpo-secure-store behind src/secrets/secureStorage.ts — device_user_id, access_token.{groupId}; lobby id list also there for now (temporary). Web has no keychain and falls back to localStorage
Server DBSupabase Postgres — groups, access_tokens, members, binds, expenses (with allocations jsonb); deny-all RLS
Server APIEdge Functions create-group, merge, fetch-entity, list-roster, rt-jwt — capability hash-check then service role
Wake channelRealtime broadcast on group:{id}; payload is tip only; rt-jwt gates subscribe (anon_channel fallback — D-006)
Hostingremote splitnext-v3 — D-001

Data model

Group

id, version, updated_at, deleted_at, name, currency_label, is_closed. Client UUID v4; merge when incoming.version > stored.version.

Member

id, group_id, display_name, version, updated_at, deleted_at. Name-slot; not a login. Soft-delete only (UI for delete/rename parked).

Bind

id, group_id, device_user_id, member_id, version, updated_at, deleted_at. Active bind = assumed member. Unique: one active bind per device per group — re-choosing re-points that bind at a higher version rather than adding a second.

Expense

id, group_id, payer_member_id, amount_cents, description, allocations, version, updated_at, deleted_at. Integer cents only. allocations is [{ member_id, amount_cents }] carried *inside* the expense (jsonb server-side), so one version number covers the whole split and a merge can never take a new amount while rejecting a share. Optional on the type: expenses recorded before slice 0007 carry none, and balances treat that as "payer credited, nobody debited".

Access token

server: token_hash, group_id, device_user_id, revoked_at. Client holds plaintext in Secure Store. One per device per group.

Every meaningful piece of behaviour, grouped by where it runs — UI, device, edge, server. Filter by kind above: what a piece is, marked by the glyph before each name. Areas run in path order; inside one, rows are ordered by weight — how many flows lean on them — so the pieces the app actually turns on come first. For how they run end to end, see Flows.

UI3

Group hub

app/group/[id].tsx 6 flows

One group's screen: shows its name, member list and everyone's balance, lets you add a member or an expense, claim a member as yourself, rename the group, and surfaces the last sync error.

Lobby screen

app/index.tsx 1 flow

The first screen: lists every group this device knows, offers Create group, and opens one into the hub.

Root layout

app/_layout.tsx 1 flow

The app shell; it starts the background catch-up sync so groups refresh on launch and on return to the app.

Device33

flushQueue

src/sync/outbound.ts:52 5 flows

Sends everything pending for a group in dependency order, keeps whatever the server did not accept, and records a typed error when it fails.

startWakeSubscription

src/sync/wake.ts:17 4 flows

Listens on the group's Realtime channel; a wake says only what changed, and this fetches that one entity. One subscription per group.

applyRemoteFetch

src/sync/inbound.ts:39 3 flows

Fetches one entity from the server and commits it, clearing or setting the group's error.

sortByFlushOrder

src/domain/version.ts:28 2 flows

Orders pending changes so parents reach the server before their children — a group before its members, a member before the bind pointing at it.

assumedMemberIdFromBinds

src/domain/assumedMember.ts:4 2 flows

Answers "which member am I in this group?" by finding this device's live bind.

computeBalances

src/domain/balances.ts:25 2 flows

Works out what each member is up or down overall — what they paid minus what they owe — most-negative first.

getGroupStore

src/store/groupStore.ts:9 2 flows

Hands out the one observable state object per group — group, members, binds, expenses, sync status, pending queue — persisted so it survives restarts, and repaired on open by normalizePersistedTimestamps.

getOrCreateDeviceUserId

src/device/deviceUser.ts:7 2 flows

The identity of this install: one id, generated once and kept in the secret store, since there are no accounts.

getAccessToken / saveAccessToken

src/secrets/tokens.ts:15 2 flows

Keeps each group's capability token in the secret store — holding it is what proves access to that group.

listLobbyGroupIds / addLobbyGroupId

src/secrets/tokens.ts:21 2 flows

The device's list of known group ids, which is what the lobby and the catch-up sync iterate over. Temporary home.

shouldAcceptVersion

src/domain/version.ts:2 1 flow

Decides who wins when two copies of an entity disagree: the incoming one, but only if its version number is strictly higher.

bindingIsOpen

src/domain/assumedMember.ts:26 1 flow

Answers "can this device still say which member it is?" — yes until the group's first live expense, which is what shows or hides the This is me button.

splitEqually

src/domain/split.ts:14 1 flow

Divides a cost equally, to the cent, across the members given. Leftover cents go out in member-id order, so two devices splitting the same cost agree exactly.

createGroup

src/sync/groupSync.ts:31 1 flow

Creates a group: writes it locally first, registers it on the server, stores the returned access token, adds it to the lobby, and subscribes for wakes.

openGroup

src/sync/groupSync.ts:269 1 flow

Opens a group for viewing — subscribes for wakes, then runs a full sync. Realtime being down does not block opening.

syncGroup

src/sync/groupSync.ts:246 1 flow

One full round trip for a group: push everything pending, pull the group back, then pull its roster. Runs alone per group so nothing races.

syncAllLobbyGroups

src/sync/groupSync.ts:256 1 flow

Syncs every group this device knows at once, isolating failures so one bad group cannot block the rest.

bumpGroupName

src/sync/groupSync.ts:85 1 flow

Renames a group: the new name shows immediately, then goes to the server as the next version.

addMember

src/sync/groupSync.ts:110 1 flow

Adds a person to the group locally, then sends them to the server.

addExpense

src/sync/groupSync.ts:146 1 flow

Records a cost: refuses anything that is not a positive whole number of cents, splits it across everyone in the group right now, writes it locally against the paying member, then sends it.

bindMe

src/sync/groupSync.ts:197 1 flow

Claims a member as this device's own person, or moves that claim to a different member — one bind per device, re-pointed rather than duplicated. Refuses once the group has an expense, or if the member is gone.

runExclusive

src/sync/exclusive.ts:4 1 flow

Queues async work per group so a push and a pull can never overlap on the same group.

shouldAttemptFlush

src/sync/queuePolicy.ts:2 1 flow

Says whether a push is worth making at all — an empty queue is a no-op, not a request.

queueAfterMergeResults

src/sync/queuePolicy.ts:23 1 flow

Decides what stays pending after a push: drop only the exact versions the server accepted, so nothing newer is lost.

applyRemoteEntity

src/sync/inboundApply.ts:18 1 flow

Works out the next local state for one incoming entity, or says no change if the local copy is already as new. Pure, so it is unit-tested.

commitRemoteEntity

src/sync/inbound.ts:19 1 flow

Writes the accepted result of that decision into the store.

pullRoster

src/sync/inbound.ts:72 1 flow

Fetches every member, bind and expense of a group and commits them one by one, so the group catches up in a single call.

useLobbyForegroundSync

src/sync/appForegroundSync.ts:6 1 flow

Runs the lobby-wide catch-up on mount and every time the app returns to the foreground.

syncError / coerceSyncError

src/sync/syncErrors.ts:5 1 flow

Gives every failure a code, a message and a timestamp, and normalises older stored errors into that shape.

initLocalGroup

src/store/groupStore.ts:53 1 flow

Seeds a freshly created group into its store as local-only, before the server knows about it.

normalizePersistedTimestamps

src/store/timestamps.ts:19 1 flow

Undoes the Date objects that reloading a saved store invents in place of our timestamp strings, so a reopened group holds exactly what a freshly synced one does.

getSecret / setSecret

src/secrets/secureStorage.ts:11 —

The one door to the device's secrets. Native goes to the OS keychain; the web build swaps in localStorage, which is why nothing wider than a per-group token belongs here.

persistPlugin

src/store/persistPlugin.ts:10 —

Where a store survives a restart: SQLite on a device, localStorage on web, so the browser target needs no wasm.

createGroupRemote

mergeEntities

src/api/edge.ts:62 1 flow

Server8

merge / mergeOne

supabase/functions/merge 2 flows

The write path: applies each pushed item if its version wins, reports accepted or rejected per item, and wakes the group's other devices.

publishWake

supabase/functions/_shared/wake.ts:11 2 flows

Tells the group's other devices that something changed, naming only what — never the data itself. A failed wake never undoes the write.

create-group

supabase/functions/create-group 1 flow

Creates the group row and issues an access token, storing only its hash.

fetch-entity

supabase/functions/fetch-entity 1 flow

Returns one entity to a caller whose token proves access to that group.

list-roster

supabase/functions/list-roster 1 flow

Returns every member, bind and expense of a group in one response.

rt-jwt

supabase/functions/rt-jwt 1 flow

Issues a short-lived Realtime token, falling back to a shared anonymous channel when it cannot.

resolveAccessToken

supabase/functions/_shared/access.ts:11 1 flow

The door: hashes the presented token and only lets it through if it is unrevoked and belongs to this group and this device.

shouldAccept

supabase/functions/_shared/entities.ts:8 1 flow

The server's copy of the version rule, deliberately identical to the client's so both sides agree on who wins.

Create group

Starts whenOn the lobby screen, the person taps Create group. Ends withThe group exists on the server, this device holds its access token, and the hub opens.
  1. UI
  2. 01
    Lobby screen calls createGroup.
  3. Device
  4. 02
    getOrCreateDeviceUserId reads this install's id from Secure Store, creating it the first time.
  5. 03
    getGroupStore opens a fresh store for the new group and initLocalGroup writes version 1 into it — the group is usable offline from this moment.
  6. Edge
  7. 04
    createGroupRemote posts the new group to create-group, which registers it and returns an access token.
    • sends { group_id, device_user_id, name, currency_label, updated_at }
    • returns { access_token, group }
  8. Device
  9. 05
    getAccessToken / saveAccessToken stores that token in Secure Store and listLobbyGroupIds / addLobbyGroupId adds the group to this device's lobby list.
  10. 06
    startWakeSubscription subscribes to the group's channel so other devices' changes arrive, asking mintRealtimeAuth / rt-jwt for permission first. If Realtime is unavailable the group still works — only live updates are lost.

Open group

Starts whenThe person taps a group in the lobby, or the hub screen mounts. Ends withThe screen shows the latest group and roster, anything pending has been pushed, and live updates are running.
  1. Device
  2. 01
    getGroupStore opens the group's store, loading whatever was saved on this device and running normalizePersistedTimestamps over it, so a reopened group is the same shape as a freshly synced one before anything reads it.
  3. UI
  4. 02
    Group hub calls openGroup for that group.
  5. Device
  6. 03
    startWakeSubscription subscribes for live updates, as in Create group step 6. A failure here is swallowed: browsing must still work.
  7. 04
    syncGroup runs a full round trip — see Sync one group.

Sync one group

Starts whenAny full refresh of one group: opening it, or the app-wide catch-up. Ends withEverything this device had pending is on the server, and the group plus its roster match the server.
  1. Device
  2. 01
    runExclusive claims the group, so a push and a pull can never overlap on it.
  3. 02
    flushQueue sends everything pending, oldest layer first.
    • sortByFlushOrder puts the group ahead of its members and members ahead of binds, so nothing arrives before its parent
    • shouldAttemptFlush stops here when the queue is empty
    • getAccessToken / saveAccessToken and getOrCreateDeviceUserId supply the proof of access
    • mergeEntities posts the batch to merge / mergeOne as [{ entity_type, id, version, payload }, …]
    • resolveAccessToken checks the token belongs to this group and this device before anything is written
    • the server applies each item through shouldAccept and, for each one it accepts, publishWake nudges the group's other devices
    • queueAfterMergeResults drops exactly the versions the server accepted and keeps the rest
    • syncError / coerceSyncError clears once the push succeeds
  4. 03
    applyRemoteFetch pulls the group row back through fetchEntity / fetch-entity, and applyRemoteEntity asks shouldAcceptVersion whether it is newer before commitRemoteEntity writes it.
  5. 04
    pullRoster pulls every member, bind and expense in one call through listRoster / list-roster and commits each one the same way.

Starts whenThe app launches, or the person switches back to it. Ends withEvery group this device knows has caught up.
  1. UI
  2. 01
    Root layout mounts useLobbyForegroundSync, which listens for the app becoming active.
  3. Device
  4. 02
    listLobbyGroupIds / addLobbyGroupId lists the known groups and syncAllLobbyGroups runs Sync one group on each in parallel, isolating failures so one bad group cannot block the others.

Starts whenOn the hub, the person types a name and taps Add member. Ends withThe person appears in the member list immediately and reaches the server on the next push.
  1. UI
  2. 01
    Group hub calls addMember with the typed name.

  4. Device

Add expense

Starts whenOn the hub, the person types an amount and taps Add expense. Ends withThe cost is listed immediately against the member who paid, reaches the server on the next push, and the This is me buttons go away — see This is me.
  1. UI
  2. 01
    Group hub parses the typed amount into whole cents and calls addExpense with the assumed member as payer.
  3. Device
  4. 02
    addExpense refuses a fraction of a cent or a non-positive amount before anything is stored, and refuses a payer who is not a member here.
  5. 03
    splitEqually divides the cost across everyone in the group at this moment, and addExpense refuses to store a split that does not add up to the total. The split is frozen into the expense: a member added later joins the next expense, not this one.
  6. 04
    The expense is written into the store at version 1, split and all, and queued — the list updates before any network call.
  7. 05
    flushQueue pushes it as one item, so the split can never arrive half-applied. sortByFlushOrder puts it after members, so the payer exists on the server before the expense that names them, and merge / mergeOne rejects it outright if that member belongs to another group.
  8. 06
    computeBalances refolds and the hub's balances move — the payer up by what they paid, everyone down by their share.

See who owes what

Starts whenThe hub is on screen and the group has at least one expense. Ends withEvery member's net position, most-negative first, with this device's own member marked.
  1. UI
  2. 01
    Group hub reads the group's members and expenses straight from the store, so the list is as fresh as the last sync and needs no network of its own.
  3. Device
  4. 02
    computeBalances credits each payer the full amount and debits each member their share. Because a split always sums to its expense, the nets cancel out across the group.
  5. 03
    assumedMemberIdFromBinds marks which row is yours; the hub colours a negative red and a positive green.
  6. 04
    Anything arriving later — a wake, a roster pull — lands in the store and the list refolds on its own.

This is me

Starts whenOn the hub, the person taps This is me on a member row. Every member offers the button while the group has no expenses, so the choice can be made and changed freely. Ends withThat member is this device's own person; the hub shows You (Name) and that row's button goes away, while the others stay offerable until the first expense.
  1. UI
  2. 01
    Group hub shows the button on every member except the one already claimed, as long as bindingIsOpen says the group has no live expense.
  3. 02
    Group hub calls bindMe with the member tapped.
  4. Device
  5. 03
    bindMe refuses once an expense exists, recording binding_closed — the UI hides the button by then, so this is the rule behind the rule, not a message anyone should normally see. A missing member records member_missing.
  6. 04
    A bind linking this device to that member is written locally and queued. If this device already had a bind, that same bind is re-pointed at the new member at the next version rather than a second one being created, so "which member am I?" never depends on which bind is found first.
  7. 05
    flushQueue pushes it, and the server rejects it unless the member belongs to the same group.
  8. 06
    assumedMemberIdFromBinds now resolves this device to that member, which is what puts You (Name) on the hub.
  9. 07
    The first expense closes it: bindingIsOpen turns false, every remaining button disappears, and the choice is fixed until some future slice offers a deliberate way to change it.

Bump group name

Starts whenOn the hub, the person renames the group. Ends withThe new name shows at once here and reaches the other devices without them asking.
  1. UI
  2. 01
    Group hub calls bumpGroupName with the new name.
  3. 02
    The name changes in the store at the next version number and is queued, so the UI never waits on the network.
  4. Device
  5. 03
    flushQueue pushes it; the server accepts the higher version and publishWake announces the change.

Peer change arrives live

Starts whenAnother device changed something while this one was subscribed. Ends withThat one entity is refetched and applied, if it is newer than the local copy.
  1. Device
  2. 01
    startWakeSubscription receives a wake naming only what changed — { group_id, entity_type, id, version }, never the data itself.
  3. 02

Slice 0007 — allocations + balances

The ledger closes: every expense carries a split that sums to its total, and the hub says who is up and who is down.

Tier — core value (foundation-risk in the merge shape) · Closed — 2026-08-07 · Tag — `slice-0007` · archive 0007-allocations-balances.md

Highlights

  • Allocations live inside the expense. One entity, one version, one merge — a device can never accept a new amount while rejecting one of its shares. The alternative (child rows per share) would have needed a transaction the entity-level merge does not have.
  • The split is deterministic across devices. Members are deduped and id-sorted, the base share goes to everyone, and leftover cents go out one at a time in that order. Two devices holding the same roster in different insertion orders produce the same allocations byte for byte, so merge cannot flap between two equally valid answers.
  • The split is frozen at record time. A member added later joins the next expense, not this one.
  • Balances are derived, never stored. computeBalances folds live members over live expenses; nothing to keep in sync, nothing to migrate.
  • A latent crash was found and fixed. Legend's parser revives exact ISO-8601 strings into Date objects on reload, so updated_at came back a different type than it went in. A one-expense group never called the sort comparator, so the bug hid from slice 0006 until a second expense existed. normalizePersistedTimestamps repairs the store at open — including stores persisted by older builds.
  • Flow clips. Seven flows record end to end against the deployed Edge Functions, with a drawn pointer so a viewer can see what is being touched. The script asserts as well as records: clean console, and balances identical across a reload.

gained the split step; gained the normalize step ahead of everything else.

  1. Device
  2. 01
    getGroupStore opens the group's store, loading whatever was saved on this device and running normalizePersistedTimestamps over it, so a reopened group is the same shape as a freshly synced one before anything reads it.
  3. UI
  4. 02
    Group hub calls openGroup for that group.
  5. Device
  6. 03
    startWakeSubscription subscribes for live updates, as in Create group step 6. A failure here is swallowed: browsing must still work.
  7. 04
    syncGroup runs a full round trip — see Sync one group.

Edge paths checked

Balancesexpense recorded before this slice (no allocations)Payer credited, nobody debited, so the visible list does not net to zero. Honest over invented: re-splitting now would attribute a debt the expense never recorded.
Balancesallocation names a member this device has not pulled yetThe share is skipped rather than shown against a blank row; the roster pull that follows corrects it.
Balancesmember soft-deleted after being allocatedTheir row, their debt and their paying all leave the fold, so the group no longer nets to zero. No UI reaches this today — member delete is parked — but the fold does not crash on it.
splitEquallyduplicate ids in the rosterDeduped before splitting, so a doubled member cannot be charged twice.
splitEquallyamount smaller than the member count (2c across 5)The first two by id owe a cent each, the rest owe nothing. Every cent is still allocated.
addExpensegroup has exactly one memberThat member pays and owes the whole amount; net zero, which is correct.
Hubno expenses yet"Nothing spent yet — everyone is square" rather than a list of zeros, so an empty group reads as empty rather than broken.
Hubreopened with two or more expensesCrashed the whole screen until fixed — see normalizePersistedTimestamps above. Latent since the persist work in 0006 and invisible with one expense, because a one-item sort never calls the comparator.
getGroupStorestore persisted before this sliceNormalized on open, so a device carrying Dates from an older build is repaired rather than left to crash.
fetchEntitywake naming an expense, stale fetch-entity deployed400 unsupported surfaced as fetch_failed on the hub and the wake was dropped; the next roster pull still caught up. Fixed by deploying the function, not by code.

Decisions

Allocations ride inside the expense entity, not as child rowsEqual split with id-ordered remainder, frozen at record timeBalances are derived on read, never storedPersisted timestamps are repaired at store open rather than by changing the persisted format

Steering

What's next

Close the hole in the ledger: an expense records *who owes*, not just who paid, and the hub shows each member's net position. Allocations ride **inside** the expense entity, so one version carries a split that always sums to its total — the invariant balances fold over.
